results.title: Live: France braces for fresh protests as social unrest enters sixth week
results.content: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests,with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

results.title: US Agriculture Department and FBI hit by cyberattacks, media report
results.content: Hackers breached systerms at the US Agriculture Department and the FBI, US media reported, amid a recent wave of major technology disruptions across the country.

results.title: House of Cards: America's enemies "no longer fear it, its allies no longer trust it'
results.content: The Economist's deputy editor Tom Standage joins us for a futuristic retrospective, taking us back to the future as we spotlight "The World Ahead 2027". We begin with the "leader of the free world", the FIFA Peace Prize recipient presiding over an America under the "Donroe Doctrine": "Its enemies no longer fear it and its allies no longer trust it in the way they did before."

results.title: Paris police officers sentenced to prison over 2020 beating of Black man
results.content: A Paris court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler, a rare such ruling. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.

results.title: Guinea bans Burkina Faso broadcaster, escalating diplomatic tensions
results.content: Tensions rise between Guinea and Burkina Faso after Conakry bans Burkinabe broadcaster RTB, amid a diplomatic dispute over gold miners and a caricature of President Mamadi Doumbouya. Meanwhile, fighting erupts between Congolese forces and the Rwanda-backed FRN group in eastern DR Congo, despite peace commitments. Finally, in Ethiopia, one entrepreneur is tackling period poverty by breaking menstrual stigma and making reusable sanitary pads more accessible.

results.title: 'Licence to kill': France adopts law presuming 'legitimate' self-defence in police shootings
results.content: French senators gave final approval on Friday to controversial legislation granting police officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when using firearms, fulfilling a long-standing demand of the far right even as weeks of student-led protests have thrust the issue of police brutality back into the spotlight. Left-wing lawmakers have vowed to challenge the bill.

results.title: 'Friends' But Who Benefits? Notes from an Historic Summit, Myanmar's Genocide Ruling, Time to 'Bre-join' the EU?
results.content: Welcome to the World This Week with Gavin Lee. You give us 45 minutes, we'll give you 7 days worth of crystal clear analysis. As ever, alongside a handpicked panel of four distinguished foreign correspondents.

results.title: Yemen's Houthis target Riyadh after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
results.content: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched strikes on Riyadh on Saturday after Saudi-led coalition air raids on Yemen, escalating a months-long surge in cross-border attacks.

results.title: 🦛 USA: Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo’s famous hippo, has died
results.content: 🦛Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo’s beloved hippo, has died aged just 9, after swallowing a knitted hat that fell into her enclosure. Born prematurely and weighing only 13kg, she captured millions of hearts around the world and became an internet sensation.

results.title: 🔴Watch live: Trump holds press conference after meeting with Xi, Putin
UK and EU strike ‘landmark’ deal to rebuild ties after Brexit
results.content: 🇬🇧🇪🇺 A fresh start after #Brexit? The #UK and #EU have agreed on a landmark #deal to rebuild ties, following a summit in Brussels this Friday. The agreement covers easier food export checks, youth mobility and carbon emission quotas.

results.title: A cultural stroll through Paris with singer-songwriters Mariam Doumbia and Zaho
results.content: Two women, two voices, two destinies: Malian performer Mariam continues her musical journey after the 2025 passing of Amadou, her partner in life and on stage. "Amadou and I sang about love. We wanted to share love with everyone. We sang of peace, of love, of justice."

results.title: ‘A more expensive EU is not a better EU’: Austria's Minister for Europe, Claudia Bauer
results.content: This week's programme hosted Claudia Bauer, Austria’s Federal Minister for Europe, Integration and Family while she was in Paris for the recent G7 meeting. She offered her thoughts on the diplomatic moves surrounding Ukraine, transatlantic relations, EU enlargement and a headscarf ban in Austrian schools that has caused disquiet. We also talked about the thorny negotiations involved in the EU’s next long-term budget: the Multiannual Financial Framework.

results.title: Trump hails 'fantastic' relationships with China's Xi, Russia's Putin after three-way talks
results.content: US President Donald Trump played up his "fantastic" relationships with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin during a White House press conference on Friday following his return to Washington after a first-ever trilateral meeting with the Chinese and Russian leaders. Here are key takeaways from his wide-ranging briefing.

results.title: Photography: A very French history
results.content: From its use as creative expression to documenting our everyday reality, photography has become an essential and widely-accessible medium since its invention. Did you know, however, that the technology was developed in France? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha takes a look at the French legacy of photography.

results.title: France investigates actor Depardieu, writer Houellebecq over alleged gang rape
results.content: French police are investigating allegations actor and convicted sex offender Gérard Depardieu raped and assaulted a woman with the complicity of bestselling author Michel Houellebecq during a 2018 film shoot, two sources following the case said Friday. The plaintiff has accused the film's director Guillaume Nicloux of being complicit in the abuse.

results.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' & 'Rivals': The big TV shows to watch this month
results.content: "Blade Runner" returns with a futuristic twist, while British bonkbuster "Rivals" is back with part two of season two. TV critic Dheepthika Laurent joins Eve Jackson to review the month’s big releases, including Netflix’s acclaimed Arctic comedy "North of North" and the lavish K-drama "Remarried Empress".

results.title: Gen Z protests spread across Europe: Mass rallies over cost of living in Spain
results.content: Protesters across Europe are set took to the streets on Friday in a show of cross-border solidarity, joining coordinated demonstrations against the rising cost of living, militarisation and other causes, in a bid to increase pressure on their governments. Protesters across Europe are set to take to the streets on Friday in a show of cross-border solidarity, joining coordinated demonstrations against the rising cost of living, militarisation and other causes, in a bid to increase pressure on their governments. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

results.title: French ex-PM Villepin announces presidential run
results.content: France's former prime minister and foreign minister Dominique de Villepin, famed abroad for his excoriating 2003 denunciation of US plans for invading Iraq, said on Friday he was running for president. Villepin enters an already crowded field of candidates seeking to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, with polls pointing towards a possible run-off between frontrunner Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally (RN) and hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon.

results.title: Shenzhen trilateral: Xi Jinping's 'masterclass in diplomatic theatre'
results.content: Xi Jinping positioned himself as a great statesman when he met with the US president and Russia's Vladimir Putin for trilateral talks in Shenzhen this week. But while the Chinese president sparkled on the world stage, does he have anything to show for it? Seong-Hyon Lee, an associate at Harvard University Asia Center, tells us how the trilateral has come up short on deliverables.

results.title: Spain’s political crossroads, Europe’s wider stakes: Spaniards to vote in key election
results.content: The stakes are high – not only for people in Spain, but also for Europe. On November 29, the country holds a parliamentary election that could see the end of the Socialist-led government and potentially a coalition between the right and the far right, in one of the EU’s biggest and most influential member states. It could also signal the end of Pedro Sanchez’s third term in office. Among other things, the prime minister may pay the political price for two shocking train crashes and the migrant crisis in Spain’s North African exclave of Ceuta.

results.title: Jamaica's beaches are increasingly off limits to locals
results.content: Jamaica usually conjures up images of white sandy beaches, Rastafari culture and Bob Marley – but another reality exists. On this small Caribbean island, less than 1 percent of the coastline is freely accessible to local people. The rest has gradually been privatised, mostly for large hotel developments and private homes.

results.title: Cincinnati Zoo's famed Fiona the hippo dies days after eating a visitor’s hat
results.content: Fiona, the hippo whose premature birth and fight for survival at the Cincinnati Zoo turned her into a global sensation nearly a decade ago, died Thursday from complications after swallowing a knit hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure. She was 9 years old. “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement.

results.title: REPLAY: Burnham, Von der Leyen hail 'turning point' in EU-UK relations
results.content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham hailed a "landmark" deal with the European Union on Friday, as the two sides sealed pacts on food exports, emissions-trading schemes and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen welcomed a "turning point" in ties with Britain following Brexit. Watch our replay.
